title: Faculty and Staff Door Signs (Credibility Poster): A Simple Schoolwide Credibility Signal
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Stuart describes a simple, schoolwide practice he encountered at Alfred G. Waters Middle School: a uniform faculty and staff door-sign template, used building-wide, that packs a surprising amount of Credibility signaling into a small physical space. Using the principal's own sign as a worked example, he breaks the template into six components - a smiling photo, years in the district, educational history, the staff member's personal "Everest" (core mission), the school mascot, and a schoolwide slogan - and explains what each one communicates to students walking the halls. He argues the power of the template lies in its uniformity: every adult in the building signals experience, competence, and shared purpose in the same visual language, reinforcing both individual and institutional Credibility. The piece ends with a broader principle about belief signals - they only take root in students' hearts through repetition that holds meaning, not through a single well-designed poster.
points: Breaks a single physical artifact - a door sign - into six discrete Credibility-signaling components: photo, tenure, credentials, personal mission ("Everest"), school identity, and slogan.
Argues the power comes from schoolwide uniformity - when every staff member uses the same template, the signal reinforces both individual and institutional Credibility simultaneously.
Frames a principal's doctorate and a teacher's personal "Everest" statement as substitutes for the old, less effective practice of framing diplomas on classroom walls.
States a transferable principle about belief signals generally: their impact correlates with how often they're repeated and how much meaning those repetitions carry, not with a single display.
quotes: As I was catching up with their principal, Dr. John Tanner, I started noticing some interesting uniformity in the building: faculty and staff door signs.
Smiling face. When kids are walking in for the first time or getting the lay of the building at the start of the year, they can associate rooms with not just names but also faces.
Number of years in the district. This indicates experience, commitment. It emphasizes that we all share being here, in this district, this year.

The school's mascot/logo. I love that this is right next to Everest; it communicates that John is both an individual with an individual mission, but he's also a member of the whole, a person after not just his agenda but OUR agenda as a school community.

The thing with slogans is that the degree to which they're lived out correlates perfectly with 1) the number of times that they are repeated and 2) the number of times that those repetitions hold meaning.
Like all belief signals, if you want to ensure a thing gets in to the heart of your listener, you have to say it and mean it again and again and again and again.
